cluster_summary: This cluster contains vulnerabilities where WebSocket or HTTP endpoints fail to properly validate the Origin header for cross-origin requests, or where authentication relies on untrusted HTTP headers (proxy-forwarded or user-supplied identifiers) without adequate checks. These flaws enable CSRF bypass, authentication bypass, or unauthorized access.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Add a route whitelist/blacklist so that proxy header authentication is only accepted for Control UI/WebSocket routes; require explicit token/password for other API routes..

mechanism.typical_fix: Add a route whitelist/blacklist so that proxy header authentication is only accepted for Control UI/WebSocket routes; require explicit token/password for other API routes.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add a route whitelist/blacklist so that proxy header authentication is only accepted for Control UI/WebSocket routes; require explicit token/password for other API routes.
sub_patterns.name: Improper trust in proxy headers for authentication without route restriction
sub_patterns.root_cause: Authentication middleware accepts proxy headers (e.g., Tailscale identity) as sufficient for all HTTP routes, including API endpoints that require token/password, without restricting to allowed UI/WebSocket routes.
